([[Baltimore, Maryland]]) | college = *[[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2014–2015) *[[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] (2016–2018) *[[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | career_start = 2019 | career_end = | years1 = 2019–2020 | team1 = [[Northern Arizona Suns]] | years2 = {{nbay|2019|end}} | team2 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years3 = 2020 | team3 = →Northern Arizona Suns | years4 = 2021 | team4 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years5 = 2022–2023 | team5 = [[Pallacanestro Varese]] | years6 = 2023–2024 | team6 = [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli Basket]] | years7 = 2024–2025 | team7 = [[Vanoli Cremona]] | years8 = 2025 | team8 = [[Sagesse SC (basketball)|Sagesse Club]] | years9 = 2025–2026 | team9 = [[JDA Dijon]] |years10 = 2026-present day | team10 = [[Elitzur Netanya]] | highlights = * [[Italian Basketball Cup|Italian Cup]] winner ([[2024 Italian Basketball Cup|2024]]) * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Defensive team (2019) }} '''Tariq Amir Owens''' (born June 30, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[JDA Dijon Basket|JDA Dijon]] of the [[LNB Pro A]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]] and [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] having transferred after his freshman year at [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]]. ==Early life== Owens mother died of pancreatic cancer when he was 14 years old.{{cite news|last1=Braziller|first1=Zach|title=How Tariq Owens' father was 'everything' for his hoop career|url=https://nypost.com/2019/04/06/how-tariq-owens-father-was-everything-for-his-hoop-career/|access-date=November 18, 2019|work=[[New York Post]]|date=April 6, 2019}} Owens attended [[St. Vincent Pallotti High School]], where he was coached by Shae Johnson. He was teammates with future [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] player [[Marcquise Reed]].{{cite news|last1=Storms|first1=Eric|title=Robert Morris transfer Marcquise Reed has led Clemson to its best season in years|url=http://dailyorange.com/2018/02/robert-morris-transfer-marcquise-reed-led-clemson-best-season-years/|access-date=April 17, 2018|work=The Daily Orange|date=March 1, 2018}} Owens spent a [[postgraduate year]] at Mount Zion Prep. He originally signed with [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio]] but was released after a coaching change.{{cite news |last1=Shaffer |first1=Jonas |title=On journey to NCAA title game, Texas Tech's Tariq Owens has come a long way since Maryland days |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2019/04/08/on-journey-to-ncaa-title-game-texas-techs-tariq-owens-has-come-a-long-way-since-maryland-days/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[Baltimore Sun]] |date=April 8, 2019}} ==College career== Owens began his collegiate career at Tennessee, playing for one season before transferring to St. John's. He averaged 5.2 points and 5.2 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2018 |title=Tariq Owens Leaving St. John's Basketball Program |url=https://redstormsports.com/news/2018/4/9/Tariq_Owens_Leaving_St_John_amp_8217_s_Basketball_Program.aspx |access-date=November 18, 2019 |website=[[St. John's Red Storm]]}} As a junior at St. John's, Owens averaged 8.4 points, 5.9 rebounds and a [[Big East Conference]]-best 2.8 blocks per game. Following the season, Owens opted to transfer as a graduate student, selecting [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]] over an offer from [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2018/04/09/st-johns-graduate-transfer-tariq-owens-pallotti-picks-texas-tech-over-maryland/|title=St. John's graduate transfer Tariq Owens (Pallotti) picks Texas Tech over Maryland|last=Markus|first=Don|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|access-date=November 18, 2019|date=April 9, 2018|archive-date=August 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815222101/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-tariq-owens-texas-tech-maryland-st-johns-0409-story.html|url-status=live}} Owens scored 18 points in a 78–63 win over [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] on November 20, 2018.{{cite news |title=Texas Tech to play Nebraska for Hall of Fame Classic title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401083477 |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 20, 2018}} As a senior at Texas Tech, Owens averaged 8.7 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game. He helped lead the Red Raiders to the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2019 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship game]].{{Cite news|last=Jones|first=Colton|url=https://www.si.com/nba/cavaliers/nba-amico/suns-sign-forward-owens-to-one-year-pact|title=Suns sign forward Owens to one-year pact|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=November 18, 2019|date=July 18, 2019}} Owens was named to the [[Big 12 Conference]] All-Defensive Team and honorable mention All-Big 12.{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Jarret |title=Texas Tech racks up Big 12 honors following championship season |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-tech/LongFormArticle/Texas-Tech-basketball-Big-12-honors-129922710/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=March 10, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Northern Arizona Suns (2019–2020)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Owens did not play in the [[NBA Summer League]] but suited up for the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On July 18, 2019, Owens signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the Suns.{{Cite news|last=Ward|first=Devin|url=https://www.kcbd.com/2019/07/20/phoenix-suns-sign-tariq-owens/|title=Phoenix Suns sign Tariq Owens|website=KCBD.com|date=July 20, 2019|access-date=November 18, 2019}} but was waived on October 15.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-waive-kramer-odiase-owens|title=Suns Waive Krämer, Odiase, Owens|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2019}} He was named to the roster of the Suns’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].{{cite news |last1=Withee |first1=Jacob |title=NAZ Suns Announce 2019–20 Training Camp Roster |url=https://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/naz-suns-announce-2019-20-training-camp-roster/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=NBA.com |date=October 27, 2019 |archive-date=November 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191123081245/https://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/naz-suns-announce-2019-20-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }} Owens had a double-double with 14 points and 15 rebounds in a 117–113 loss to the [[Texas Legends]] on November 12.{{cite news |last1=Bergner |first1=Brian |title=NAZ Suns rally late, but fall to Legends 117–113 |url=https://www.dcourier.com/news/2019/nov/13/naz-suns-rally-late-fall-legends-117-113/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[Prescott Valley Tribune]] |date=November 13, 2019}} On January 5, 2020, Owens led the team in scoring with 18 points to go with nine rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across in a 101–93 victory over the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], helping snap a 13-game losing streak for Northern Arizona.{{cite news |title=Tariq Owens: Leads team in scoring |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tariq-owens-leads-team-in-scoring/ |access-date=January 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 5, 2020}} ===Phoenix Suns (2020)=== On January 15, 2020, the [[Phoenix Suns]] announced that they had signed Owens to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-tariq-owens|title=Phoenix Suns Sign Tariq Owens|date=January 15, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 15, 2020}} In his NBA debut on February 2, Owens scored two points and grabbed two rebounds in a 129–108 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news |title=Antetokounmpo lifts Bucks over Booker-led Suns 129–108 |url=https://www.nbc15.com/content/news/Badgers-light-up-St-Cloud-State-in-11-1-win-567512991.html |access-date=February 2, 2020 |work=WMTV |date=February 2, 2020}} ===Long Island Nets (2021–2022)=== On January 27, 2021, Owens was included in the roster of the [[Long Island Nets]], who mentioned that the returning right to Owens had been acquired from the [[Northern Arizona Suns]] along with returning right to [[Matt Farrell]] in exchange to returning rights to [[Joe Cremo]] and [[Drew Gordon]] earlier during off-season trades.{{cite web|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-2021-roster|title=Long Island Nets Announce 2021 Roster|date=January 27, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 27, 2021}}
